title: Battery replacement and lithium safety
summary: How lithium batteries fail, how to handle them safely, and what to do in an emergency.

sections.heading: Why lithium batteries are dangerous
sections.body: A phone battery packs a lot of energy into a thin pouch. If the pouch is punctured, crushed, bent or overheated, it can short inside and start a fire that is hard to put out. This can happen minutes after the damage, so a battery that looks fine may not be safe.

sections.heading: Spotting a bad battery
sections.body: A failing battery may drain very fast, shut the phone off early or make the phone hot. A swollen battery is the clearest danger sign. It may push the back or the screen away from the frame. Never charge or keep using a swollen battery, and take it to a repair shop instead of opening it yourself.

sections.heading: Handling rules
sections.body: Discharge the battery to below 25% before you remove it. Use plastic tools only. Never bend, dent or heat the battery directly. Use the pull tabs slowly, or loosen the adhesive with isopropyl alcohol. Fit only a battery made for your exact model, from a seller you trust.

sections.heading: If something goes wrong
sections.body: If a battery hisses, smokes or gets hot, drop it into a metal container of dry sand if you can do it safely. Then move away and let fresh air in, and do not breathe the smoke. If there is a fire, leave the room and call emergency services. Your safety matters more than the phone.

sections.heading: Disposal
sections.body: Cover the connector with non-conductive tape. Keep the old battery in a non-flammable container away from anything that can burn, until you can take it to an e-waste or battery collection point. Never put a lithium battery in household trash.

quiz.question: You notice that a battery is swollen. What should you do?
options: Keep using it until it stops
Stop, and take it to a repair shop
quiz.explanation: A swollen battery is a fire risk. Do not charge it, press it or try to remove it yourself.

quiz.question: Below what charge level should a battery be before you remove it?
quiz.explanation: A battery with less charge holds less energy, so it is less dangerous if it gets damaged.

quiz.question: A battery starts to hiss and smoke. What is the right response?
options: Hold it under your face to check it
Put it in sand if safe, move away and let air in
quiz.explanation: Get distance and fresh air. If there is a fire, leave and call emergency services.

quiz.question: How should you get rid of an old lithium battery?
options: Tape the connector and take it to a collection point
quiz.explanation: Lithium batteries can start fires in trash trucks and dumps, so always use a collection point.
